observations: body L1-L10: the end of Porphyry's words begun on p. 305; the addendum to pp. 305–306 (p. LXXIX, al-Būnī) is recorded on p. 305. «Sahl ibn Bishr», «‘Alī Ibn Abī ’r–Riǵāl», «‘Alī ibn Riḍwān» (L3), «Ptolemaeus» and «Albatenianis» are letter-spaced; the long dash of «’r–Riǵāl» measures 4.9 pt. The n of «opinio» and of «universitatis» (L4) prints broken, and a speck prints after «‘Alī» (L7). Ptolemy's numbers as reported by ‘Alī ibn Riḍwān (the Sun 17, the Moon 12 1/2, Saturn 10, Jupiter 12, Mars 7 1/2, Venus 8, Mercury 7) agree with al-Battānī's (p. 130, L11-L13 of the translation: the Sun 15, the Moon and Jupiter 12, Venus 8, Mars, Mercury and Saturn 7) only for Jupiter, Venus and Mercury, as printed.

body L11-L16: the dash after «c)» measures 10.1 pt; the dash of «15–19» (5.2 pt) is a long dash. A heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition (L12); the dots after «stellis» are five, and the » after them prints faint. The last i of «maximi» (L14) prints broken, like an exclamation mark. A and B lie 90° from both P and Q, so each is a pole of the great circle through P and Q, and AQ = QB = 90°, as printed.

body L17-L24: the figure of the quadrature stands on the left of L17-L22, redrawn from the print: the arcs A P′ B and A R P B as circles fitted to the ink (rms 0.26 and 0.27 pt), the ecliptic AB as a straight base, and RS and P′Q perpendicular to it; the letter P beside P′Q prints faint and broken and is set whole. Both «P′» of L17 are printed with the same prime. The dots after «quadraturam» (L18) are six. «Al–Battānī» (L20) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.2 pt). The place is p. 131, L15-L19 of the translation, which reads «... nec a 90° unquam differt, sive magna sive parva est latitudo; idque in globo super cuius polos circuli incidunt manifeste cognoscitur»; L18-L19 and L23-L24 give it in indirect speech, with «sive parva sive magna» and «in sphaera, supra cuius polos».

body L25-L29: in the triangle RSA, right-angled at S, cos RA = cos RS cos AS; with RA = 60°, cos AS = cos 60° : cos RS, which exceeds 1/2 when the latitude RS is not zero, so AS < 60°; with RB = 120°, cos SB = −cos AS, so SB = 180° − AS > 120°, as printed. The dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 9.6 pt; a heavy bracket closes the addition.

body L30-L37: «Ibn Yūnus» (L30, L37), «Caussin» and «al–Battāni» (L31) are letter-spaced; the long dash of «al–Battāni» measures 5.2 pt, and its last letter is printed as a dotted i, not ī. The Arabic word of L33 reads فظيع, as printed. With RA = RS = 60° the same relation gives cos AS = 1 and AS = 0: the sextile ray falls on S, as printed. The figure of the sextile ray stands on the right of L33-L37, redrawn from the print: RS with its round top at R; RA; the dotted circle about R through A (its centre found 1.0 pt from R, its radius 39.5 pt against RS 39.2 pt), dash by dash, touching the ecliptic at S; the ecliptic, which left of S prints thinner (0.1 to 0.7 pt) and broken in places. RS prints broken a little above its middle. A speck stands under the d of «radiatio» (L36).

notes_left L1-L8: «Zahel», «Suter» (divided between L4 and L5), «Steinschneider» and «Albohazen Haly» are letter-spaced. «saec» (L4) and «p» (L5) are printed without a full stop. The dash before «Auctor» measures 7.7 pt; «15-16» and «39-46» have hyphens (3.1 and 3.7 pt).
notes_right L1-L8: the hyphen of «pos-» (L2) prints as a point. An ink blot stands after «pag. 20.» (L5). «Καρπός» (L8) is set as printed, with the final ς.
